name: The Workbench
tagline: Production tools as single HTML files — a DAW, a vector editor, a spreadsheet. Take over mid-demo.
_note: A product demo you can seize control of is a different object from a product demo you watch. That is the only reason this channel exists. No video files: each entry drives the real tool in an iframe.

videos.title: A DAW, a vector editor and a spreadsheet — three files, no install, and you can grab the mouse
videos.description:
Every software demo on the internet has the same flaw: the person driving never makes your mistake. You cannot ask it a question. You watch someone else's cursor find someone else's menu.

So here are three genuinely large tools — a multitrack DAW with a piano roll and a WAV exporter, a vector editor with a boolean geometry kernel, and a spreadsheet with a real calculation engine and dynamic arrays — driven live, in an iframe, on the same clock as any other video on this site.

Pause on the mixer and drag a fader. Pause on the pen tool and draw something wrong. The demo will wait, because the demo is the application.

Combined, the three files come to 598 KB. That is roughly two seconds of 4K video.

card.title: A demo you can interrupt.
card.note: Nobody's cursor but yours has to find the menu. Pause anywhere and the tool is simply open, with the demo's state still loaded.

lower.title: Browser DAW Studio
lower.bench: multitrack · piano roll · drum sequencer · WAV export · 135 KB
lower.fix: Audio needs a gesture, so the script provides one — then the demo song plays for real

scenes._note: The four workspace tabs share a class and differ only by label, so they are addressed by text. Web Audio will not start without a real gesture — the player's click is a real gesture, which is why this works at all.

lower.title: Vector Design Studio
lower.bench: boolean geometry kernel · layers · multiplayer stub · 199 KB
lower.fix: Tools, snapping and zoom are all real controls — pause and draw over the demo file

scenes._note: Tools are chosen with the keyboard — R, O, L, V — not by opening the shape menu. The first version clicked the ▭ button, which opens a dropdown rather than selecting a tool, and every drag after it went straight through the open menu. Measured after the fix: three scripted drags, three new rows in the LAYERS panel.

lower.title: HyperSheet
lower.bench: from-scratch calc engine · dynamic arrays · charts · 264 KB
lower.fix: The grid is a canvas, the ribbon is real — click a cell and the formula bar follows

scenes._note: Cells are painted into a canvas, so a cell cannot be addressed by selector at all — it is selected the way a person selects one, by dragging across it.

videos.title: Programming an 808 pattern live — the sequencer is running while you watch it
videos.description:
A full production suite in one file: drum machine, synthesizer, sampler, effects rack, vocoder and an auto-play arranger.

The script starts the transport, randomises a pattern, and moves through the racks while the sequencer keeps running underneath. Nothing is pre-rendered — the audio is being synthesised in your browser as the playhead moves, which is why the pattern is different every time the randomiser is hit.

And because it is the real instrument, the obvious thing to do is stop the video and program your own sixteen steps. There is an EXPORT PATTERN button. It will give you the JSON.

Headphones, obviously.

card.title: Synthesised, not rendered.
card.sub: Every hit you are about to hear is generated on your machine.
card.note: Which is why the randomiser gives a different pattern on every run — there is no mixdown to play back.

videos.title: Three generative studios where the output is different every single run
videos.description:
The strongest case for publishing a program instead of a recording is art that is never the same twice.

Aurora Veil is a magnetic field you shape with the pointer, with charged particles falling into it — drag anywhere and the curtains follow. Snowflake Symmetry grows a crystal under a temperature and humidity model, six-fold, one branch at a time, and no two are alike. The Library of Babel is Borges' library rendered as navigable hexagons containing every book that could ever be written.

A video of any of these is a single sample from an infinite set. This is the set.
